questions.q: What makes an integration "inbound" rather than "outbound"?
options: An external system pushes data into ServiceNow, rather than ServiceNow initiating the call
It always uses SOAP instead of REST
It only applies to integrations built with IntegrationHub
It requires a MID Server in every case
questions.explain: Inbound means the external system initiates the data movement into ServiceNow — the opposite of outbound, where ServiceNow initiates the call.

questions.q: A nightly payroll extract arrives as a flat file from a system that cannot make outbound HTTP calls. Which inbound mechanism fits, and why?
options: A Scripted REST API, because it's the more modern approach
An Import Set, because it fits batch data and systems that can't call an API directly
A REST Message, because ServiceNow needs to initiate the call
An IntegrationHub spoke action, because spokes always handle file-based data
questions.explain: Import Sets, built on staging tables and a Transform Map, are designed exactly for batch data arriving from a system that can't push data in via an API call.

questions.q: What does an IntegrationHub spoke action actually wrap, according to this lesson?
options: A MID Server installation
An Import Set Transform Map
One or more REST Messages, packaged into a reusable, drag-and-drop action for Flow Designer
A completely different mechanism unrelated to REST Messages
questions.explain: IntegrationHub doesn't replace REST Messages — a spoke action wraps one or more of them so a Flow can reuse the integration without hand-writing HTTP details each time.

questions.q: In the monitoring-tool-creates-an-Incident example, what makes this integration event-driven rather than a simple scheduled check?
options: ServiceNow polls the monitoring tool every few seconds asking if anything changed
It uses SOAP instead of REST
It requires a human to manually trigger the Incident creation
The outage itself is the event, and the Incident is created immediately as a reaction to it, not on a fixed schedule
questions.explain: Event-driven integration reacts the moment something happens, rather than either side repeatedly polling to ask if anything has changed.

questions.q: Which three questions does this lesson say actually settle an integration pattern choice?
options: Which programming language is used, how large the company is, and the ServiceNow instance version
Whether the integration uses JSON, how many fields are involved, and the time zone of the external system
Who initiates the data movement, how real-time it needs to be, and whether the external system can make outbound HTTP calls at all
The cost of the external system's license and the number of ServiceNow admins on staff
questions.explain: Those three questions — initiator, real-time need, and outbound call capability — are exactly what points to inbound vs. outbound vs. batch vs. event-driven.
